Conversations to score the metrics on, e: Conversations to score. Each is {"call_id": "<uuid>"} for a production call or {"test_result_id": <int>} for a simulated one. Conversations already in the lab are skipped.
How Bluejay reaches the agent in simulat: How Bluejay connects to the agent in simulations. If you leave it out, Bluejay picks it from the connection field you send, such as `vapi_assistant_id` for `VAPI`. Anything else defaults to `PHONE`.
Agent variables, e.g. {\"account_number\: Variables for the agent, such as {"account_number": "A-111"}. Every digital human of the agent inherits them to fill `{{name}}` tokens. A trait or override on the digital human wins. Send {} to clear.
The digital humans to create (1 to 100),: The digital humans to create, 1 to 100. Each item is checked on its own. A rejected item is listed in `errors` and the rest are still created.
The digital humans to create: one object: The digital humans to create: one object or a list of 1 to 100. Each item is checked on its own. A rejected item is listed in `errors` and the rest are still created.
Items the server rejected; every other i: Items the server rejected. Each has `index` (its position in the list you sent), `status_code` and `detail`. Everything else was still created.
Headers sent only when Bluejay downloads: Headers Bluejay sends when it downloads `recording_url`, such as {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"}. They are used once and never stored or logged. Use a short-lived token.
Deprecated: use recording_url (with reco: Deprecated. Use `recording_url`. The recording as a base64 data URL (.mp3, .mp4, .wav or .m4a). Voice agents only.
Extra JSON stored on the conversation (G: Extra JSON stored with the conversation. Set `external_conversation_id` to your own ID to update the conversation later. Sending the same ID again replaces it and is billed again.
Agent version number the call ran agains: The agent version the call ran on. If you leave it out, Bluejay uses the version labeled production.
What the alert watches: custom_metric (o: What the alert watches: `custom_metric`, `standard_metric`, `custom_goal`, `metadata_field`, `system_failure` or `issue`. It decides what `entity_field` holds.
The exact thing watched, per entity_type: The specific thing to watch. For a metric, its UUID. For `metadata_field`, the metadata key. For `system_failure`, `status:<status>`. For `issue`, `any` or one issue's UUID.
Where to send notifications when the ale: Where to send alerts, as a list of {"type", "target"}. Types are email, slack, webhook, pagerduty, betterstack and incidentio. Leave it out for no notifications.
The window the alert is judged over. For: How far back the alert looks. For observability alerts, seconds of recent conversations. For simulation alerts, how many recent runs must all meet the condition. Defaults to 600 seconds or 1 run.
When the simulation runs. Pick one form: When the simulation runs. Pick one: every N minutes or hours, daily, weekly, monthly, or a cron expression. Times use the schedule's timezone.
Conversations to score the metrics on, e: Conversations to score. Each is {"call_id": "<uuid>"} for a production call or {"test_result_id": <int>} for a simulated one. Send [] to add conversations later.
Chart options. Pie: {\"slice\": \"<label: Chart settings for the chart type. Pie: `slice`, `clamp_pct` and `label`. Line, bar and histogram: `benchmark` draws a reference line. KPI: `compare_previous: false` hides the change. `unit` adds a unit after values.
What the widget plots; required unless c: What the widget plots. Required unless the chart type is `table`. Each item is {"metric": <key>}, such as `call_count`, `latency`, `custom_metric`, `goal`, `tool_call` or `trace_attribute`. Add `threshold_operator` and `threshold_value` to chart the share of conversations that meet a condition.
The conversation graph as a JSON object: The conversation graph as JSON with `nodes` and `edges`. Every node and edge needs its own string `id`. Edges also need `source` and `target`. Send {"nodes": [], "edges": []} for an empty draft.
A five-field cron expression (minute hou: A five-field cron expression, such as `0 9 * * *` for 9:00 every day. It uses the schedule's timezone, or UTC if none. Day-of-week counts Monday as 0, so use names like `mon-fri`.
Past calls to rebuild as digital humans. Give each the transcript or a production `conversation_id`, plus how closely to replay it. Use `mode: strict` to reproduce a production call.
Number of digital humans to generate fro: How many digital humans to generate from the agent's system prompt rules. It must be even. Each rule gets one caller the agent should help and one it should refuse.
Case facts applied to EVERY generated di: Facts shared by every generated digital human, such as a test account number. Facts for one caller go on that digital human. Only use things a real caller could say out loud.
The scenario the digital human enacts, i: What this caller wants, in one or two sentences. Facts the caller knows go in `traits`, exact lines in `scripted_responses`, and who speaks first in `speaks_first_config`.
The pass/fail condition for this one tes: How to tell this test passed, in one or two things the transcript can show, such as 'the agent verified the member ID and booked a callback'. Describe what the agent does, not the caller. Leave empty if you use `enriched_playback`.
Who this caller is, in one short line (e: Who the caller is, in one short line, such as 'retiree on a family plan, not comfortable with phone menus'. What they want goes in `intent`.
Case facts THIS CALLER holds and can rec: Facts this caller knows and can say when asked, such as member ID, date of birth or order number. Only use things a real caller would know. Things the agent looks up or should say do not belong here.
The 'if the agent says X, the caller doe: Exact replies the caller gives when the agent says something specific, such as a fixed line, a keypad entry or a pause. Each row pairs `match_phrase` with a response.
Who opens the call, and the caller's ope: Who speaks first, and the caller's opening line if it must be fixed. Check `dynamic` before setting a custom message.
A past call already split into turns, ea: A past call split into turns. Each turn has a `role` (`USER` or `AGENT`) and an `utterance`. The caller's lines become what the digital human says. Replay can use `start_offset_ms` and `end_offset_ms` to talk over the agent where the caller did.
Mocked tool results for this test case,: Fake tool results for this test case, by tool name, such as {"check_availability": {"slots": ["Thursday 7:40 AM"]}}. They apply only when mocking is on for the agent, and they win over the agent-level setting.
For a red-team digital human, its broad: The broad attack type for a red-team digital human. Usually set from `attack_vector`. Values: `recon`, `social_engineering`, `prompt_injection`, `text_native`, `audio_native`, `content_harm`.
Who reaches out first on this leg, seen: Who starts this leg. `inbound` means the customer contacts the agent. `outbound` means the agent does. Leave it out to use the agent's own direction. An outbound SMS leg can't follow another SMS leg.
Labels to add or remove, e.g. ['producti: Labels to add or remove, such as `production` or `staging`. Matching ignores case. `latest` is managed for you. `production` can't be removed. Move it to another version instead.
Turn tool mocking on or off for every si: Turn tool mocking on or off for every simulation on this agent. Live traffic is never mocked. On ElevenLabs agents, turning it on creates a hidden branch named `bluejay-mocks`, and turning it off archives it.
How closely the digital human follows th: How closely the digital human follows the original call. `strict` repeats the caller's lines. `smart` reuses them where they fit and improvises otherwise. `persona` keeps only the situation and goal.
How match_phrase is compared to the agen: How `match_phrase` is compared to what the agent says. `exact` is a fuzzy text match and costs nothing. `context` asks an LLM whether the meaning is the same, for when the agent could word it many ways.
An utterance the AGENT would say, which: A line the agent would say, such as 'Can I have your account number?'. Write the line you expect to hear. A description of what the agent is doing never matches. An empty string fires on the caller's next turn when `scripted_responses_ordered` is set.
The conversation: status, digital_human_: The full conversation: status, duration, transcript, audio, metric results, tool calls and trace IDs.
With speaks_first on: wait up to 5s for: Wait up to 5 seconds for the agent to speak first, and speak only if it stays quiet. If the agent greets, a custom opening message is dropped. Turn it off to always say the opener.
Optional overrides as a JSON object: nam: Optional settings as a JSON object, such as `name`, `max_levels`, `max_total_dhs`, `max_call_duration_minutes` and `hangup_on_transfer`. Values above the limits are lowered. Leave it out for the defaults.
generated: Bluejay writes a realistic re: `generated`: Bluejay writes a realistic result. `fixed`: returns your `response`. `real`: not mocked, your tool runs.
The fact's name, as the agent would ask: The fact's name as the agent would ask for it, such as `member_id` or `date_of_birth`. Names are shared across your organization, so reuse an existing one. Only use things a caller would know.
What the alert watches: custom_metric (o: What the alert watches: `custom_metric`, `standard_metric`, `custom_goal`, `metadata_field`, `system_failure` or `issue`. It decides what `entity_field` holds. Leave it out to keep the current one.
The exact thing watched, per entity_type: The specific thing to watch. For a metric, its UUID. For `metadata_field`, the metadata key. For `system_failure`, `status:<status>`. For `issue`, `any` or one issue's UUID. Leave it out to keep the current one.
Where to send notifications when the ale: Where to send alerts, as a list of {"type", "target"}. It replaces the whole list. Send [] to stop all notifications. Leave it out to keep the current list.
For observability or all alerts, how man: How many matching conversations in the window trigger the alert, or a percent if `min_events_type` is `percentage`. Ignored for simulation alerts. Leave it out to keep the current one.
Replacement timing; overwrites the store: When the simulation runs. Pick one: every N minutes or hours, daily, weekly, monthly, or a cron expression. Times use the schedule's timezone. It replaces the current timing. Leave it out to keep the current one.
The scenario the digital human enacts, i: What this caller wants, in one or two sentences. Facts the caller knows go in `traits`, exact lines in `scripted_responses`, and who speaks first in `speaks_first_config`.
How much the digital human varies its ow: How much the digital human varies its wording. Lower it to get the same call twice, for regression tests. Keep it higher for exploratory or red-team cases.
When and how the digital human ends the: When and how the digital human ends the call, in your own words. This replaces the built-in behavior, so only write for a case it would miss. Send `default` to go back.
Case facts THIS CALLER holds and can rec: Facts this caller knows, such as member ID or order number. Listed traits are updated and others stay, unless `traits_mode` is `replace`. Call `get_digital_human` first to see the stored ones.
How `traits` apply when you send traits: How `traits` applies on update. `merge` (default) updates only the listed traits. `replace` deletes all stored traits first, then saves only the list.
The 'if the agent says X, the caller doe: Exact replies the caller gives when the agent says something specific, such as a fixed line, a keypad entry or a pause. If you send this, it replaces the existing list.
Who this caller is and how they come acr: Who this caller is and how they come across, such as 'retiree on a family plan, not comfortable with phone menus'. What they want goes in `intent`.
Who opens the call, and the caller's ope: Who speaks first, and the caller's opening line if it must be fixed. Check `dynamic` before setting a custom message. If you send this, it replaces the current setting.
One entry per widget to place: {\"widget: One entry per widget to place: {"widget_id": "<id>", "layout": {"x", "y", "w", "h"}}. Widgets you leave out stay where they are.
Extra filters, on top of the dashboard's: Extra filters that limit which conversations the widget counts, on top of the dashboard's own filters. Send [] to remove them. Leave it out to keep the current one.
Chart options. Pie: {\"slice\": \"<label: Chart settings for the chart type. Pie: `slice`, `clamp_pct` and `label`. Line, bar and histogram: `benchmark` draws a reference line. KPI: `compare_previous: false` hides the change. `unit` adds a unit after values. Leave it out to keep the current one.
The complete metric list; it replaces ev: The full list of metrics. It replaces every existing metric, so resend the ones you want to keep. Each item is {"metric": <key>}, such as `call_count`, `latency` or `custom_metric`.
A complete replacement graph with `nodes: The full replacement graph with `nodes` and `edges`. It overwrites the stored graph, so start from what `GET /v1/scenario/{workflow_id}` returns. Leave it out to keep the current one.
The health checks each run grades, as a: The health checks each run grades. Three are built in (`connection`, `agent_malfunction`, `latency`). Your own checks use a custom metric or a digital human. Each has an `id`, `label`, `description` and `enabled`. At least one enabled check needs a `checkType`.
Where DOWN and recovery alerts go: an ob: Where DOWN and recovery alerts go: `slack`, `pagerduty`, `betterstack`, `incidentio` and `email`, plus `notify_on_recovery` (default true). Leave it out for no alerts.
Replacement for the whole checks list; c: The full checks list. Changing it rebuilds the monitor's simulation. The health checks each run grades. Three are built in (`connection`, `agent_malfunction`, `latency`). Your own checks use a custom metric or a digital human. Each has an `id`, `label`, `description` and `enabled`. At least one enabled check needs a `checkType`.
Replacement for the whole notifications: The full notifications object. It replaces the current one. Leave it out to keep it.
